In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular mechanisms that underlie insulin resistance and the development of atherosclerosis in order to find ways to prevent these conditions and their consequences.
the development of new drugs for the treatment of diabetes and related disorders, with a particular interest in the role of the liver in the pathogenesis of these conditions.
the development of a novel approach for the treatment of dyslipidaemia and the associated risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
inhibition of MTP by a small molecule inhibitor improves insulin sensitivity and lowers the atherogenic risk associated with diabetic dyslipidaemias.

chronic inhibition of microsomal triacylglycerol transfer protein (Mtp) in the genetically diabetic dyslipidaemic Zucker fatty rats improves insulin sensitivity and significantly reduces atherogenic risks.

chronic inhibition of intestinal MTP with a specific, orally bioavailable inhibitor improves insulin resistance and reduces atherogenesis by reducing intestinal lipid synthesis and enhancing the hepatic clearance of chylomicrons in Zucker fatty rats.
